why: phase-476 W2 — registers a timer whose callback is a C function pointer and whose capture the executor arena holds: the road a C++ lambda takes, the timer twin of `add_arena_subscription_c_callback_with_capture`. The capture's bytes go in the timer entry's trailing region and an optional drop hook destroys them on release, so the C++ side keeps a two-word handle and no heap cell. rclcpp type-erases the callable into a `std::function` the timer owns; ours has no allocator on that path.
